news.headline: Florida: Two New Marijuana Legalization Initiatives Filed for 2028
news.summary: Two new proposed constitutional amendments to legalize adult-use marijuana were filed with Florida officials this week for the 2028 ballot. One was approved by the Division of Elections on September 30 and the other is awaiting a financial impact review; both would let existing medical dispensaries sell to adults 21 and older, and both are separate from Smart & Safe Florida's older initiative, which the state now lists for 2028. For patients, adult-use legalization is no longer possible before 2028, and the proposals would change how the market is licensed and who can sell.

news.headline: IRS Whistleblower Office Reviewing Claim Over $10 Million Florida Money Trail Tied to Anti-Marijuana Campaign
news.summary: The IRS Whistleblower Office is reviewing a claim filed by Florida Rep. Alex Andrade about $10 million in state Medicaid settlement money that ended up funding opposition to the 2024 marijuana legalization amendment. It matters to patients and advocates because it keeps the question of how that campaign was funded under federal scrutiny, though a review is not a finding of wrongdoing.

news.headline: FL Monthly Puff: New Florida Market Entrants With 22 New Vertical Licenses Granted
news.summary: This October market roundup recaps the Department of Health's September 11 final order granting 22 new vertically integrated medical marijuana licenses, which closed the April 2023 application round. It also reports a proposed OMMU limit on celebrity endorsements and Curaleaf deal and store news; those last items are unconfirmed by an official source and mostly predate October. More licensed operators could mean more dispensary locations and competition over time.
